name: NJ-10
label: Safe D

key_factors: District's D+27 partisan lean toward Democrats
Massive fundraising gap: McIver raised $2.1M and holds $814K, while Bucco raised about $2,300
Incumbent McIver is running and prediction markets price a Democratic hold as certain
model.rationale: The forecast rests on the district's heavy Democratic lean and a nearly total resource mismatch: the incumbent has more than $800,000 on hand while the challenger has raised roughly $2,300. With no public polls and no expert ratings, markets and fundamentals both point to an easy Democratic hold.
model.watch: With no polling in this race, the forecast depends entirely on fundamentals, so an unexpected candidate development or an unusual national swing would be the only way it tightens.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
New Jersey's 10th District, anchored in the Newark area, is a heavily Democratic seat with a D+27 partisan lean, and LaMonica McIver is running for re-election as the incumbent. Races in districts this lean rarely become competitive in general elections, and nothing in the available evidence suggests otherwise here.

The Republican challenger, Carmen Bucco, has run a nominal campaign, raising about $2,300 with barely $1,000 on hand. McIver, by contrast, has raised roughly $2.1 million and holds $814,000 in cash, and outside groups have spent only lightly on her behalf. No public general-election polls are available, and no expert raters have flagged the race. Prediction markets price the seat as a certain Democratic hold, and the fundamentals point the same way.
